_comment: Gemma 4's multi-token-prediction drafter (`Gemma4AssistantForCausalLM`, Google's `-it-assistant` repos). Unlike a Qwen3.5 head it ships as its own checkpoint with its own config, so it names its target config (`head_targets`: its stem -> `<arch>/<stem>`). Google publishes no target checkpoint that carries it: its drafter is always a repo of its own, which its model card loads by name (`assistant_model`). So the drafter a target drafts with by default names the repo each compiled variant of it loads from (`published_as`, a drafter checkpoint loading only into the variant of its own precision): it compiles beside its selected target under `mtp-heads` (on with `metal`), and serving a checkpoint of that target's shape with no `--speculative-model` loads that repo. 26B-A4B's is Google's drafter at MLX 4-bit g32, the one #237 measured (2.16 tokens a step greedy over 8 prompts; its variant compiles under `mlx-affine-b4-g32`, which `quant/mlx` selects): on the MLX 4-bit target (base M5, one request, greedy, against the target alone's 20.9 ms a token) it reads 11.5 ms on a repetitive reply and 17.6 on a code prompt. Google's bf16 drafter accepts as many drafts but reads every draft's 262k-row lm_head at bf16, and decodes prose slower than the target alone (26.5 ms). The QAT drafter pairs with the QAT target: on this one it accepts fewer (1.90 tokens a step, #237) and on a repetitive reply none (0 of 128, where the g32 one accepts 85 of 90). The others compile under `spec/mtp` and draft when `--speculative-model` names them. The target's facts it needs come from its `.overrides.json`: the target's layer count (its KV pool's geometry) and the target layers whose KV it reads. It has NO K/V of its own (`num_kv_shared_layers` = all its layers): its attention reads the target's KV of the target's last sliding and last full layer (`reads_target_kv`). It borrows only its target's embedding (`borrows`), placed under `target_embed_tokens`; its logits are its own tied 262k x 1024 embedding's, read as the `lm_head` linear straight from `model.embed_tokens` (renamed: the drafter never reads its embedding as one). `pre_projection` / `post_projection` sit at the checkpoint's top level (`top_level_weights`). mlx sets the attention `scale = 1.0` for both classes, as the target's. Rope scalars are nested per class under `rope_parameters`, aliased to the flat names as the target's.
